subject: Re: Redwood integration for GitHub - discovery & demo coordination
messages:
From: Leo Ramos <leo@codecraft.io>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interest in Redwood for GitHub integrations + migration questions

Hi Evelyn,

I signed up for Redwood earlier this week (trial) — been poking around the self-serve UI and tried the quick-start GitHub App install. We like what we see but have some questions before booking a deeper walkthrough: 

- We're a mid-size infra team at CodeCraft Labs; ~120 repos (mix of public and private), monorepo on some services.
- We're evaluating moving some CI/observability from GitLab -> GitHub; how does Redwood handle repo-level permissions and installation across orgs? Any migration patterns you recommend?
- Webhook delivery: does Redwood provide retries/backpressure insights when GitHub sends bursts?
- Auth model: can we use our org-managed GitHub App or do we have to use OAuth per-user?
- Performance: we expect high-rate events during CI spikes — curious about rate-limits, batching, and autoscaling behavior for GitHub-backed flows.

If helpful I can loop in our CTO Amanda for a technical call. Ideally we'd do a 30–45 minute demo focused on the GitHub integration and webhook reliability. I dropped a few notes in the trial account as well.

Thanks,
Leo Ramos
Engineering Manager, Platform
CodeCraft Labs
attachments: (none)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Leo Ramos <leo@codecraft.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in Redwood for GitHub integrations + migration questions

Hi Leo — great to meet you, and thanks for signing up.

Short answers up front: Redwood supports org-scoped GitHub Apps (recommended for org-wide installs), we surface install/permission diffs for multi-org setups, and the runtime includes webhook retry tracking + a delivery metrics dashboard. For high event rates we use adaptive batching and a backpressure circuit that falls back to a compatible model variant and queues safely — happy to show this.

Would you and Amanda be open to one of these slots for a focused 30-minute technical walkthrough (agenda below)? If none work, tell me your timezone and a couple times and we'll accommodate:

- Wed Jul 22, 10:00–10:30 PT
- Wed Jul 22, 13:00–13:30 PT
- Thu Jul 23, 09:00–09:30 PT

Pre-demo asks (quick):
- Approx count of private vs public repos and any org/enterprise installs you already have.
- Whether you plan to keep self-hosted runners or migrate to GitHub-hosted CI during the roll-out.
- Any specific compliance or IP controls we should include in the call.

I've attached a short integration checklist that lists the common permission scopes and recommended install patterns — it also has a place where you can paste the trial Org ID so we can pre-check installs ahead of the call.

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf (stub)

Agenda (30min)
- 5m quick intros and goals
- 10m GitHub app/permissions + install patterns
- 10m webhook delivery, batching, autoscale, and observability demo
- 5m Q&A & next steps / PoC plan

Marissa (cc) will send a calendar invite once you confirm slot and attendees. Soojin — adding you as the OSS integrations lead for technical detail.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — that looks great.

We can do Wed Jul 22 but need to shift to 13:30 PT (15 minutes later) — conflict with standup. Amanda (CTO) will join; she wants to touch on migration pattern and security boundary for private repos. We have ~85 private / 35 public repos. We currently use a mix of self-hosted runners and GitHub-hosted for some teams; migration is phased.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood's GitHub App requires organization admin to install or whether repo admins can grant install for specific repos? That's one of our procurement blockers.

—Leo
